scope: Constructor comparison of the delivered English drafts; not independent validation
output_format_relation: The two output_format strings are identical and express the shared definition summarized in rules.json.

predicates.cg: Return a compact table of their stated claims; this is not an assessment of proof correctness or algorithm applicability.
predicates.go: Return a compact table of their stated claims; this is not an assessment of proof correctness or algorithm applicability.

predicates.cg: Read the complete ZO-SCG bullet in the constrained-optimization discussion, including its continuation up to the next bullet. Include every work cited there.
predicates.go: The scope is the complete ZO-SCG bullet in the constrained-optimization discussion, including its continuation up to the next bullet. Include every work cited there.

predicates.cg: Resolve the bibliography entries to original arXiv works and merge entries only when they represent the same work.
predicates.go: Bibliography entries that represent the same original arXiv work belong in a single row; merge entries only when that identity is established.

predicates.cg: Use official submission histories as observed on 12 September 2026.
predicates.go: Use official submission histories as observed on 12 September 2026.

predicates.cg: For each work, use the latest arXiv version posted no later than the survey v2 posting on 21 June 2020 at 06:40:13 UTC.
predicates.go: For each work, use the latest arXiv version posted no later than the survey v2 posting on 21 June 2020 at 06:40:13 UTC.

predicates.cg: Use older versions with a referenced title only to establish identity.
predicates.go: Use older versions with a referenced title only to establish identity.

predicates.cg: the first main-text theorem, in document order, that bounds the Frank–Wolfe gap for the work's own zeroth-order conditional-gradient method without requiring objective convexity.
predicates.go: the first main-text theorem, in document order, that bounds the Frank–Wolfe gap for the work's own zeroth-order conditional-gradient method without requiring objective convexity.

predicates.cg: Use its nonconvex part where the theorem has separate parts.
predicates.go: Use its nonconvex part where the theorem has separate parts.

predicates.cg: Read the statement together with its associated algorithm, query definitions and gap definition.
predicates.go: using the statement, associated algorithm, query definitions and gap definition.

predicates.cg: Report the theorem locator, declared query model, operation on the random gaps and exact iterate range.
predicates.go: The table should identify that theorem and describe its declared query model, operation on the random gaps and exact iterate range

predicates.cg: Use the main statement and its associated algorithm to report these fields, even when proof passages differ. Preserve what is printed rather than repairing it.
predicates.go: Use the main statement and its associated algorithm to report these fields, even when proof passages differ. Preserve what is printed rather than repairing it.

predicates.cg: Exclude results for other algorithms or convex-only cases. Do not derive rates, validate proofs or decide whether an algorithm should be applied.
predicates.go: Exclude results for other algorithms or convex-only cases. Do not derive rates, validate proofs or decide whether an algorithm should be applied.

predicates.cg: Use the quantity that the paper denotes as its gap, without correcting its definition.
predicates.go: Use the quantity that the paper denotes as its gap, without correcting its definition.

predicates.cg: Preserve the printed indices, including any shift between a gap index and its iterate. Do not exchange minimum and expectation or substitute a last-iterate gap.
predicates.go: Preserve the printed indices, including any shift between a gap index and its iterate. Do not exchange minimum and expectation or substitute a last-iterate gap.

predicates.cg: Return only a pipe-separated table with header ARXIV_ID|VERSION|THEOREM|QUERY_MODEL|GAP_FORM|ITERATES.
predicates.go: Return only a pipe-separated table with header ARXIV_ID|VERSION|THEOREM|QUERY_MODEL|GAP_FORM|ITERATES.

predicates.cg: Use one row per distinct work, ordered by its first citation occurrence in the complete bullet. Retain distinct works with identical claims; there is no winner or tie selection.
predicates.go: Use one row per distinct work, ordered by its first citation occurrence in the complete bullet. Retain distinct works with identical claims; there is no winner or tie selection.

predicates.cg: ARXIV_ID is the original identifier as a string, without an arXiv: prefix or version suffix. VERSION is v followed by the official version number.
predicates.go: ARXIV_ID is the original identifier as a string, without an arXiv: prefix or version suffix. VERSION is v followed by the official version number.

predicates.cg: THEOREM is the numbered theorem locator, including a part number when needed, in the form Theorem n.m or Theorem n.m(p).
predicates.go: THEOREM is the numbered theorem locator, including a part number when needed, in the form Theorem n.m or Theorem n.m(p).

predicates.cg: QUERY_MODEL is SAMPLE_FUNCTION for sampled loss values with the same sample reused at the finite-difference query points, or EXACT_FUNCTION for values of a fixed function even when the gradient estimate uses random directions. Classify the declared model, not a noiseless special case of a sample model.
predicates.go: QUERY_MODEL is SAMPLE_FUNCTION for sampled loss values with the same sample reused at the finite-difference query points, or EXACT_FUNCTION for values of a fixed function even when the gradient estimate uses random directions. Classify the declared model, not a noiseless special case of a sample model.

predicates.cg: GAP_FORM is EXPECTED_UNIFORM_GAP for the expectation of the paper's gap at an iterate selected uniformly from the reported range, or EXPECTED_MIN_GAP for the expectation of the minimum of the paper's gaps over that range.
predicates.go: GAP_FORM is EXPECTED_UNIFORM_GAP for the expectation of the paper's gap at an iterate selected uniformly from the reported range, or EXPECTED_MIN_GAP for the expectation of the minimum of the paper's gaps over that range.

predicates.cg: ITERATES gives that inclusive range in the paper's iterate variable, using notation such as w_2..w_(M-1).
predicates.go: ITERATES gives that inclusive range in the paper's iterate variable, using notation such as w_2..w_(M-1).

predicates.cg: Use UNKNOWN for inaccessible, absent or ambiguous evidence in any non-key cell, and retain the row. If an arXiv identity is unresolved, use CITE_n as ARXIV_ID, where n is the survey reference number; do not infer a merge. Do not use NONE.
predicates.go: Use UNKNOWN for inaccessible, absent or ambiguous evidence in any non-key cell, and retain the row. If an arXiv identity is unresolved, use CITE_n as ARXIV_ID, where n is the survey reference number; do not infer a merge. Do not use NONE.

numeric_thresholds: No rate or accuracy threshold is part of this revision. The temporal cutoff and the source's symbolic iterate boundaries are explicit in both variants.
procedural_difference: CG supplies three short retrieval/reading steps. GO specifies the same literature comparison and source-selection requirements without prescribing an execution sequence.
